title: Impact of the 2026 Financial Reporting Changes on Digital ID Uptake

sections.body: Cabinet of Barbados · Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology · Paper code K(A) · For decision

sections.heading: 1. Matter for consideration
sections.body: The Ministry of Finance’s new financial reporting rules, announced on 5 February 2026, add quarterly disclosure steps for capital projects [3]. Applied to the NDIF, they would delay disbursement by up to two quarters, slowing digital identity uptake just as public registration is meant to scale [5]. This paper asks Cabinet to exempt the NDIF from the new cycle until Q1 2027.

sections.heading: 2. Decision requested
bullets: approve $15 million from the Contingency Reserve for the NDIF;
designate the National ID Act Amendment Bill a legislative priority;
authorise the Minister to agree revised milestones with the World Bank.

sections.heading: 3. Background
sections.body: The National Digital Identity Framework (NDIF) was approved in 2022 to move paper-based identity systems onto a secure national digital platform [1]. The policy is approved, but procurement is 14 weeks behind because of cross-departmental data integration [2].
sections.tail: The delay risks breaching Clause 4.1 of the World Bank Development Loan (P.L. 345/2023), which requires substantial progress by the end of Q1 [4].

sources: Nation News – “ID rollout faces reporting hurdle”

messages.text: Refer to the Ministry of Finance changes to financial reporting announced on 5 February 2026. Draft a policy paper showing how they could slow the uptake of digital identity among the public in Barbados. I’ve attached a few sources to start from.
Your first draft is ready. I filled all five sections from your two files, three links and the Directory, and cited each claim. Review the highlighted assumptions before sharing.
